executive_assessment.text: The 2026 CCDR identifies named districts where flood exposure overlaps poverty, with Sabah/Sarawak tenure, monitoring and institutional-coordination constraints adding subnational depth.

The ISIS note describes a conditional displacement/protection–resource-tension mechanism, not measured climate-caused violence. Adaptation recommendations and national-plan development are not verified delivery.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2026 reports: Flood and poverty exposure overlap in Sarawak’s Kanowit, Kapit, Sibu and Song districts and coastal Sandakan, Semporna, Sabak Bernam and Batu Pahat; poorer households have weaker housing and fewer savings or insurance.
Source dated 2026 reports: Indigenous land-tenure insecurity in Sabah and Sarawak leaves customary rights contested and undermines forest governance and conservation.

Source dated 2026 reports: The CCDR proposes targeted housing, livelihood and financial support for poorer flood-prone communities and climate planning with women, youth, Orang Asli and other Indigenous peoples.
Source dated 2026-08-10 reports: Floods displaced 129,000 people in 2021 and 156,000 in 2022, concentrated in five states; poorer Klang Valley households can be trapped in repeated evacuations.
Source dated 2026-03 reports: Sabah’s climate governance is centralized in the Chief Minister’s Department; Sabah and Sarawak have overlapping mandates and silos that impede coordination.
Source dated 2026-03 reports: Sabah uses iForSABAH, GeoForest and forest-fire danger maps, while both Borneo states report technical and budget gaps in climate monitoring.
Source dated 2026 reports: During the first half of 2026, dry spells lowered paddy yields by over 60% in areas of Kedah, Perlis and Perak.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification. Routine/default app-use approval does not certify claims or sources. 11 of 12 evidence records and 1 of 1 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
No inspected source establishes climate stress as the cause of organized armed violence in Malaysia; ISIS describes conditional displacement-related social-tension pathways.
The reviewed evidence does not show active insecurity disrupting climate adaptation; the Indigenous tenure finding concerns governance and conservation.
The full World Bank Flood Risk Management report PDF exceeded the fetch limit; its landing-page summary and search snippets were not used.
The 2026 institutional overview covers Sabah and Sarawak, not the national climate-adaptation system; proposed Climate Change Centers were not yet established.
World Bank CCDR recommendations are proposals, not evidence that services or resilience measures have been delivered.
The policy note's legal-protection framing is attributed to its authors and date, not adopted as a comprehensive current legal finding.
Customary tenure, coordination and trust constraints are relevant governance mediators but do not establish armed conflict or an observed insecurity blockage to adaptation.
Routine/default app-use approval granted by Lindsey Jones on 2026-10-27; independent source verification remains incomplete. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
